title: Move a bulky wall-wart power brick to the end outlet of a crowded power strip so a fourth cord can plug in
instruction: Plug the black cord on the right into the power strip, leaving everything already on the strip plugged in.
context: Nearly everyone has run into a crowded household or desk power strip where a wide AC wall-wart transformer brick was plugged into an interior socket so its overhanging body covers the neighbouring empty socket. Because the light plastic power strip is free-standing on the desk and already powers two connected cords that must not be unplugged, adding one more cord requires steadying the strip with one hand while unplugging the bulky wall-wart with the other, moving the wall-wart one socket over to the end outlet so its body hangs harmlessly past the end of the strip, and plugging the new cord into the newly uncovered interior socket.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top z = 0). Strip mat: fixed charcoal non-slip rubber with low 0.45 cm corner alignment cleats, 16.0 x 28.0 x 0.4 cm, centred at (24.5, -2.0). Cord mat: fixed olive-slate non-slip rubber, 14.0 x 9.0 x 0.4 cm, centred at (24.5, -18.5). Power strip: an unwired 4-outlet NEMA 5-15R desk power strip (Woods / GE compact strip, $8.99; ivory ABS housing 5.4 cm along x by 22.2 cm along y from y_rel = -9.8 to +12.4 cm by 3.0 cm tall, 360 +/- 5 g free-standing on the strip mat at (24.5, -2.0), red rocker switch bezel at y_rel = +8.4 cm, four grounded 3-slot NEMA 5-15R receptacles along the top face at 3.40 cm pitch: Outlet 1 at y_rel = +4.2 cm, Outlet 2 at +0.8 cm, Outlet 3 at -2.6 cm, and end Outlet 4 at -6.0 cm; each outlet has two polarized blade slots at x_rel = -0.45 cm, y_slot = y_outlet +/- 0.635 cm and a round ground bore at x_rel = +0.65 cm). Pre-seated cords: Outlet 1 holds a blue molded NEMA 5-15P appliance plug (3.0 x 2.5 x 2.8 cm, 48 g, rear +x cord boot) and Outlet 2 holds an identical grey molded NEMA 5-15P plug; Outlet 3 holds a white bulky AC wall-wart adapter brick (TP-Link 12V 1.5A adapter, 3.6 cm along x by 5.4 cm along y by 4.0 cm tall with a 4.2 x 3.6 x 0.3 cm top bezel lip, 105 +/- 3 g; its 3 NEMA 5-15P prongs sit 1.0 cm from its +y face so its 4.4 cm -y body overhang spans y_rel = -7.0 to -1.6 cm, completely covering end Outlet 4 at y_rel = -6.0 cm). Loose black appliance cord: a black molded 3-prong NEMA 5-15P plug (3.6 x 2.4 x 3.8 cm head with a 4.2 x 2.4 x 0.3 cm top pull-cap lip, 1.45 cm tapered brass blades and 1.60 cm ground pin, 64 g), resting prongs-down at (24.5, -18.5) on a fixed teal desktop cord cradle (4.6 x 4.4 x 1.85 cm side ledges) so the 1.60 cm ground pin hangs 0.25 cm clear above the mat. Both arms start at READY.
scoring: The trial's score is evaluated at its final step (SCORE_OVER = end; zero permanent positive latches). Permanent 0.0 failure latches: (a) existing_unplugged: either pre-seated appliance plug (Outlet 1 blue plug or Outlet 2 grey plug) is pulled > 0.60 cm above the strip top face or out of its socket at any step; (b) strip_tipped: the free-standing power strip tilts > 25.0 deg, drifts > 6.0 cm from (24.5, -2.0), or drops off the table. Let strip_undisturbed hold when the power strip rests upright (tilt <= 8.0 deg) within <= 3.0 cm of (24.5, -2.0). Let plug_in_outlet(plug, k) hold when a plug sits coaxially in Outlet k with |dx|, |dy| <= 0.55 cm, face gap between -0.25 cm and +0.50 cm of the +3.0 cm strip top face, relative tilt <= 8.0 deg, and relative yaw <= 12.0 deg. End-step tiers (given no failure latched and strip_undisturbed + Outlet 1 & Outlet 2 still seated): 1.00 when the white wall-wart is seated flush in end Outlet 4 (uncovering Outlet 3), the black cord plug is seated flush in Outlet 3, every finger pad of both arms is >= 3.0 cm clear of the power strip, wall-wart and black plug, and strip, wall-wart and black-plug linear speeds stay < 0.8 cm/s continuously over the final 1.0 s (20 steps at 20 Hz); 0.75 when all four plugs (1, 2, black plug in 3, wall-wart in 4) are seated flush on strip_undisturbed at the end step before >= 3.0 cm hand clearance or 1.0 s stillness is met; 0.50 when the wall-wart is seated flush in end Outlet 4 (uncovering Outlet 3) while the black plug is not yet seated flush in Outlet 3; 0.25 when the wall-wart has been pulled clear of Outlet 3 (> 2.2 cm laterally or > 1.8 cm vertically) without yet seating in Outlet 4 (or if the black plug took Outlet 3 leaving the wall-wart unplugged); 0.00 otherwise. Real trial post-run checks, in order: (1) Active-plug & strip check (from trial video + ruler): if Outlet 1 or Outlet 2 ever lifted > 6 mm, or if the strip tilted > 25 deg or slid > 6 cm from its mat mark (or sits > 3 cm off mark / > 8 deg tilted at the end), score 0. (2) Four-outlet feeler & video stillness check: check Outlet 1 (blue), Outlet 2 (grey), Outlet 3 (black), and end Outlet 4 (white wall-wart overhanging the -y end) with a 5.0 mm feeler gauge between plug face and strip face: if all four pass <= 5.0 mm face gap and trial video confirms both grippers stayed >= 3.0 cm clear with zero visible motion over the final 1.0 s, score 1.0; if all four pass <= 5.0 mm face gap but a gripper is < 3.0 cm away or still moving in the final 1.0 s, score 0.75; if Outlets 1, 2 and wall-wart in 4 pass <= 5.0 mm while black plug is unseated, score 0.50; if Outlets 1 and 2 pass and Outlet 3 was cleared of the wall-wart without seating wall-wart in 4, score 0.25; otherwise score 0.
reset_notes: Between trials (< 15 s): hold the power strip down, pull the black plug out of Outlet 3 and set its body prongs-down onto the teal desktop cord cradle at (24.5, -18.5), pull the white wall-wart out of end Outlet 4 and press it flush back into Outlet 3 (so its -y overhang covers Outlet 4), verify the blue and grey plugs in Outlets 1 and 2 sit flush, and align the power strip inside its (24.5, -2.0) mat cleats. In real trials the power strip's own supply plug is left disconnected from wall mains.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with convex-hull PhysX contact at 240 Hz; all four NEMA 5-15R receptacles have true 3-cavity polarized blade slots and ground bores in the strip housing (>= 3.8 mm per-side PhysX clearance for reliable rigid-body insertion while blocking 180 deg reversed ground pins and wall-wart overhang collisions; real spring-clip contact retention of ~15-25 N is higher than pure rigid side-wall friction). Mains current is not simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (600 steps: reaches directly toward the black plug on the right cradle without moving the overhanging white wall-wart from Outlet 3 to Outlet 4); demo: 1.0 (seed=0 in 442 steps, seed=1: 1.0; move_wart_only: 0.50; unplug_existing: 0.00)
